draft.title: Atomic structure
card: An atom has a small, dense nucleus at its centre. The nucleus holds protons and neutrons. Electrons move around the nucleus.
positive charge, found in the nucleus. Neutron: no charge, found in the nucleus. Electron: negative charge, found outside the nucleus.
The atomic number is the number of protons. It decides which element the atom is. The mass number is the number of protons plus neutrons.
A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons, so the charges cancel. Neutrons = mass number - atomic number.
draft.remember: Atomic number counts protons. Mass number counts protons and neutrons.

a.q: An atom has 11 protons, 12 neutrons and 11 electrons. What is its mass number?
a.why: Mass number = protons + neutrons = 11 + 12 = 23. The number 11 is the atomic number, which counts protons only. Electrons are not counted in the mass number.
a.clue: Add the particles that sit in the nucleus.

b.q: An atom of an element has a mass number of 40 and an atomic number of 18. How many neutrons does it have?
b.why: Neutrons = mass number - atomic number = 40 - 18 = 22. Adding the two numbers gives 58, which is wrong because the mass number already includes the protons.
b.clue: The mass number already includes the protons.
